title: Machine Learning: Classification Metrics from Scratch
summary: Implement accuracy, the confusion matrix, precision/recall/F1 and macro-F1 without scikit-learn - the metrics every ML interview probes.
problemStatement:
## Scenario
You are on an ML team that cannot pull heavy libraries into a tiny evaluation service. Implement the core **classification metrics** by hand in `metrics.py`.

## Task
Implement these functions (labels may be ints or strings; inputs are equal-length lists):

- `accuracy(y_true, y_pred)` - fraction of exact matches.
- `confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=None)` - returns a nested dict `{actual: {predicted: count}}` containing **every** label in `labels` as both a row and a column (zero-filled). Default `labels` is the sorted union of the labels seen in `y_true` and `y_pred`. Pairs involving a label not in `labels` are ignored.
- `precision_recall_f1(y_true, y_pred, positive_label=1)` - returns `(precision, recall, f1)` treating `positive_label` as the positive class. Any ratio whose denominator is `0` is `0.0`.
- `macro_f1(y_true, y_pred)` - the unweighted mean of the per-class F1 over every label seen in `y_true` or `y_pred`.

## Errors
Every function raises `ValueError` if `y_true` and `y_pred` differ in length or are empty.

requirements.title: Accuracy and input validation
requirements.description: accuracy() is correct and every function rejects mismatched or empty inputs.

requirements.title: Confusion matrix
requirements.description: Zero-filled nested dict over all labels, respecting an explicit labels argument.

requirements.title: Precision, recall and F1
requirements.description: Binary metrics with safe handling of zero denominators.

requirements.title: Macro F1
requirements.description: Unweighted mean of per-class F1 across all labels seen.
